chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ribat, from Abd al-A'la, the mawla of Al Sam, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah عليه السلام: I stumbled and my nail broke off, so I placed a bandage upon my finger. So how should I perform wudu (ablution)?
He said: This and what resembles it is known from the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.
Allah has said: “He has not placed upon you in the religion any hardship.”

key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution); the ritual purification being asked about
key_terms.امْسَحْ: wipe; the practical instruction given for the covered injury
key_terms.حَرَجٍ: hardship; undue difficulty removed by divine law
key_terms.ظُفُرِي: my nail; the injured body part mentioned in the question
key_terms.كِتَابِ اللَّهِ: the Book of Allah; the Qur'an as the source of the ruling
key_terms.مَرَارَةً: a bandage or protective covering placed over the injury

ai.seo_question: How should wudu be performed if a finger is injured and covered with a bandage?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for wudu (ablution) when an injury prevents normal washing, instructing the person to wipe over the covering on the injured finger. The Imam عليه السلام grounds this ruling in the Qur'anic principle that Allah has not placed hardship in the religion, showing how legal ease is derived from the Book of Allah.
